Raised in California's San Fernando Valley, he took over his father's building company and partnered with Naseeb Saliba to expand into major public works. He later combined Tutor-Saliba with Perini, retaining a substantial stake in the contractor.

long_biography.plain_text:
Ronald Tutor chose government contracting because he disliked continually seeking outside investors for property developments. Beginning with small Navy, county and school projects in 1965, he built a business around public works. His approach required estimating the cost of constructing precisely what the client's plans and specifications demanded.

At the University of Southern California, Tutor combined financial support with practical involvement in its campus centre. He helped oversee the design and his firm constructed the building, which opened in 2010. Designed by AC Martin, it brings meeting rooms, classrooms and dining facilities around a courtyard with open walkways facing the shared space.
